div.head: Forf 2
div.ab: Be forfencge. Embe forfang witan habbað gerǽdd, þæt man ofer eall [Engle]land gelíc[n]e dom healde: þæt is æt men fiftene peningas ⁊ æt horse healswá, sy hit ofer ane scire, sy hit ofer má, ðe læs ðe unmihtig man feorr for his agenon swince ⁊ eac to feola sylle.

De forefang (id est preuencione uel anticipatione) decreuimus, ut per totam Angliam idem iudicium teneri debeat, hoc est de homine XV denar. et de equo similiter (reddantur), sit ultra unam schiram (unum comitatum), sit ultra plures, ne homo inpotens longe pro suo proprio laboret (fatigetur) et etiam nimis det.

De anticipacione sapientes consiliati sunt, ut per totam regionem simile iudicium teneatur, id est: pro homine XV nummi, pro equo tantumdem, siue ultra unum comitatum siue ultra plures, ne forte inbecillis et longe pro suo laboret necnon et nimium tribuat.

Von [Lohn für] Wiederergreifung. Betreffend Einfangen [von Gestohlenem] haben die Witan bestimmt, dass gleiches Gesetz über ganz England (das ganze Land B Cons.) gehalten werde: nämlich [Eigenthümer zahle dem Retter] für [jeden zurückgebrachten] Sklaven 15 Pfennig, und für ein Pferd ebenso, sei es über Eine Grafschaft hin [zu verfolgen gewesen], sei es über mehrere hin, damit nicht ein unvermögender Mann um sein Eigen [wieder zu erlangen] weithin sich mühe und auch nicht zu viel zahle.

Of [the reward for] recovery. Concerning the seizing [of stolen goods] the witan have decreed that the same law be kept over all England (the whole land, B, Cons.): namely [let the owner pay the rescuer] 15 pence for [each recovered] slave, and the same for a horse, whether [it had to be pursued] across one shire or across several, lest a man without means should toil far for his own [property] and also pay too much.

Of seizure/recovery: Wise men have decreed that throughout all England the same judgement holds: that is, 15 pennies for men and also for horses, be it over one shire or several, lest a man of small means is burdened by long journeys to recover [the objects of] his own labour.[?]

div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; A later addition (c. 1000), already placed here in the archetype of B, the Quadripartitus and the Consiliatio (so before 1100), related to II Atr App. 8.3 and 9. The heading is in red. ‘Engle’ is in a later hand and was also missing in the Consiliatio, but is probably original; the ‘n’ of ‘líc[n]e’ is written above in a later hand. ‘healswá’: compare ‘his’ II Cn 75 (so not ‘healf’). Liebermann compares Forf 1.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 389, October 2026 (MS Cons)
